observation: Across the first ten completed campaigns (Executor v86) and the three healthy v98 campaigns, protocol adherence and correctness were perfect everywhere: every evaluated candidate passed all five validation cases with inputs unchanged and max_abs_error at float rounding scale. Eleven campaigns across six workload families (normalization, backward, reduction, gated activation, in-place and multi-state optimizer update, chained attention contraction) ended no_qualified_candidate at maximum_turns without reaching the 1.05 materiality ratio - per_channel_moments evaluated twelve candidates without approaching it, so the ceiling is not a candidate-count artifact. The v98 contraction batch broke the pattern: gemm_silu produced the first qualified endpoint of the series, so the saturation claim is scoped to the elementwise/reduction/optimizer/normalization families at these shapes, and the contraction family - where the baseline materializes a whole operand per program - is where within-vocabulary headroom lives, matching F-2026-09-10-010 on the B300 route.
proposed_change: Read this as saturation of within-vocabulary optimization, not as a provider-capability result: prefer capability ticks (vocabulary/lowering coverage such as tile_loops, richer access indices, multi-stage reductions) over expecting provider-side improvement inside the current vocabulary at these shapes. Before the next sweep, freeze one fixed baseline bundle per task so successor revisions report baseline movement separately from candidate headroom.
verification_plan: Standing observation to re-measure each tock: rerun the same ten tasks on each successor revision with the frozen baseline bundles and compare the candidate-minus-baseline gap series.
